text:
Alex Kim: Heads up — several scanner pipelines started failing after yesterday's IAM role rotation. Trivy jobs throwing KMS decrypt errors and GHAS findings are being suppressed unexpectedly. Anyone triaging?

Maria Santos: Saw this too. Error from one worker: 
```
2025-02-15T03:18:22Z ERROR scanner/worker: decrypt failed: rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = requestor does not have permission to perform kms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt on projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/scanner/cryptoKeys/key-scanner
```

scanner-bot: Scan job #4521 failed: KMS_DECRYPT_PERMISSION_DENIED (retry scheduled)

Samir Patel: FYI an org-policy change went in at 03:12 UTC that removed broad service account bindings from a few roles. Might be related. @Alex Kim can you paste the role binding diff from terraform?

Alex Kim: Quick diff from infra apply: 
```
- role: roles/cloudkms.cryptoOperator members: - serviceAccount:scanner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
+ role: roles/cloudkms.cryptoOperator members: []
```

Julie Park: Also noticing GHAS results aren't attaching to PRs anymore — suppression rules in our scanner pipeline appear to be matching new SBOM path patterns. So we might have two regressions: perms + overly-broad suppression.

Maria Santos: Repro steps locally: 
1) export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=~/.gcp/scanner-sa.json
2) run `./scripts/run-trivy --kms-key projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/scanner/cryptoKeys/key-scanner`
Observed: `AccessDenied: Permission denied for cryptoKey`
Service account is scanner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com (checked in secret manager).

Samir Patel: Short-term mitigation: re-add `kms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt` (or kms:Decrypt equivalent) to the scanner service account for that key, then kick the failed jobs. Medium-term: update terraform to pin the SA binding and add a CI smoke test that performs a dummy decrypt.

Alex Kim: On it — I'm going to re-add the binding and retry the jobs. I'll also start a suppression audit; if regexes are too broad they might be silencing new GHAS fingerprints.

Samir Patel: Assigning owners: @Maria Santos to verify the KMS perms fix and smoke test; @Julie Park to audit suppression rules and SBOM path changes; @Alex Kim to coordinate infra rollback/patch and retry failing pipelines. ETA 2h?

Maria Santos: I can validate in ~30m and then re-run the CI smoke job.

scanner-bot: Scan job #4521 retried by Alex Kim — status: SUCCESS

Alex Kim: Update: re-added decrypt binding, scans are back online. Suppression audit found 12 GHAS findings suppressed by a rule that matches `^/src/.*test/.*` — our SBOM generator started normalizing test paths into `/src/test/...` which made the rule hit more cases. Opening PR to narrow the regex and add unit tests for the suppression matcher.

Julie Park: I'll open the suppression PR and include test vectors. Also flagged an actual vuln: webapp pulls jquery 3.4.1 (CVE-2024-XXXX) — that's a high-severity dependency we should patch in next deploy. Marking as P1 with immediate patch window.

Samir Patel: For prioritization matrix reminder: critical RCE in running containers -> P0, high remote code execution or data exfiltration libs -> P1, medium -> P2. Add jquery patch to P1, schedule in the next sprint, but if exploit evidence appears, escalate to P0.

Alex Kim: Created issue #3443 on security board linking infra change, suppression PR, and the jquery upgrade. I'll follow up with a short postmortem if anything else flaps. Thanks all :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: @oncall paging — KMS binding was restored; monitoring shows no further decrypt errors in the last 15m.

Maria Santos: Verified — local smoke decrypt passes and CI job passed. Closing immediate incident. Next actions: (1) infra PR to pin SA binding and add decrypt smoke test, (2) suppression PR to narrow regex + tests, (3) dependency PR for jquery upgrade. I'll add owners and timelines to #3443.

Alex Kim: Great. Leaving follow-ups on the board; will schedule a quick 15m sync if suppression PR needs discussion.

Julie Park: Thanks team.
